newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London lose gains as Dow falls.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London lose gains as Dow falls.

text.p: Hong Kong shares trading in London were dragged into negative territory by T-bonds and Wall Street on Wednesday after earlier powering to record levels in the aftermath of the Hang Seng's dramatic rise.

"We were up 140 at one time but we're back," one dealer said. "We've been following London and the Street and the long bond. The long bond was the main reason Hong Kong was up today so one can only guess it will come off tomorrow, although the long bond hasn't closed yet."
By 1500 GMT the Hang Seng London Reference index was 11.91 points lower at 13,754.74.
The Dow was down 17.32 points at 6,744.97 and the March long bond future was 9/32 weaker at 111-4/32. London's FTSE 100 was down 13.9 points at 4,154.3.
Earlier, the Hang Seng London index hit a record high of 13,902.86, in the wake of Hong Kong's gains. The Hang Seng in Hong Kong reached a record close of 13,766.65, up 472.78 points or 3.56 percent.
"The move last night just shocked people," one dealer said.

"People are rather reluctant to jump in at these sort of levels but at the same time they would be concerned about going short of anything, given the way it moved and the way futures closed," he said. "So we seem to be in no-man's land."
